newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish C.Bank chief says rate rise likely in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Polish C.Bank chief says rate rise likely in 1997.

text.p: National Bank of Poland (NBP) President Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz told a news conference on Monday the central bank would wait for preliminary December inflation data to decide on its official interest rates but said a rise might be unavoidable.

"We won't cause any surprises before the holidays, we will wait for some working figures on inflation in December...which is not a typical month because of vast demand for cash...but everything indicates that such a decision will be unavoidable," Gronkiewicz-Waltz said.
She said a sign that the bank's lombard and discount rates, now 25 and 22 percent respectively, should be higher, would be a rise in market rates to levels close to the bank's official rates.
"It will be a very clear signal that our rates have to be increased...if market rates will come close to ours," she said.

Gronkiewicz-Waltz said the bank's rate rise might be forced by ballooning credit for households, which she said was likely to grow 100 percent this year. Corporate credit grew 31 percent in the first 11 months of the year.
"It is the same situation as with the currency reserves boom in 1995 -- it is not the growth itself but its pace which is worring us," she said.
"The role of the NBP is an unpleasant one ... it is similar to the role of a person who comes to a swinging party and takes away the punch bowl," Gronkiewicz-Waltz said.
